US AI regulation just collapsed with a phone call.

Three tech CEOs — Mark Zuckerberg, Elon Musk, and David Sacks — called the president directly in the hours before he was set to sign a new AI safety executive order. The order was scrapped. A White House source told Axios the president 'just hates regulation.'

There will be no comprehensive federal AI safety framework in 2026.

But here is what most people are getting wrong: the absence of federal regulation does not create clarity. It creates fragmentation. States will write their own rules. The EU already has its framework. Sector-specific regulators will step in. The result is a patchwork that is harder to navigate than a single standard.

In the same week, the Vatican announced its first-ever encyclical on AI. Governance pressure is not disappearing — it is shifting from legislatures to institutions and culture.

For business leaders, the move is clear: build internal AI governance now, before external rules force reactive compliance.
